stories.headline: Jim Rohn’s 70/30 Rule: Why Financial Planning Trumps Income
stories.summary: The article challenges the assumption that higher income automatically leads to better financial outcomes, citing 'business philosopher' Jim Rohn's 70/30 money rule. It emphasizes that effective budgeting and strategic planning are more critical to wealth accumulation than raw earnings alone.
stories.original_title: Wealth wisdom: “If I had more money, I would have a better plan. My mentor responded ...” said the author of ‘7 Strategies For Wealth & Happiness’, - check this smart budgeting rule so you have more money — Do you also believe that having more would mean that you will have a better plan? Well, if you do, you might be wrong. 'Business philosopher’ Jim Rohn's 70/30 money rule explains why financial planning matters more than income. Read on to know budgeting rules…
stories.context: Many people believe that if you just earn more money, you will automatically become wealthy, but this is often not true because spending habits usually rise to match income. Jim Rohn was a famous motivational speaker who taught that how you manage your money matters much more than how much you make. His "70/30 rule" suggests that you should spend no more than 70% of what you earn and save or invest the remaining 30%. This simple habit ensures that you are building wealth over time rather than just living paycheck to paycheck, regardless of your salary size.
stories.why_it_matters: This reminds people that making more money doesn't automatically make you rich. If you spend everything you earn, you stay broke. Learning to save and plan is the real key to building wealth.
stories.other_side: Some argue that low wages are the main problem. They say you can't budget your way out of poverty if you don't earn enough to cover basic needs.

stories.headline: Ontario’s Auto Strategy Fails as Subsidies Prove Ineffective
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Ontario's current automotive industry strategy is obsolete, noting that declining employment makes continued financial subsidies to preserve jobs economically unsound. The author advocates for ending these subsidies to allow market forces and entrepreneurship to drive the sector.
stories.original_title: Opinion: Ontario’s tired auto strategy doesn’t work anymore — As industry employment declines, shovelling money in to preserve jobs makes less and less sense. Stop the subsidies and cue the entrepreneurs
stories.context: Ontario is a Canadian province that has long relied on its car manufacturing industry, offering government money (subsidies) to keep car factories open and jobs secure. However, recent reports suggest that despite this financial help, the number of auto jobs is still dropping, meaning the government is paying billions for a shrinking workforce. Critics argue that this approach is outdated and that the money would be better spent helping workers transition to new industries rather than propping up a declining sector. The debate centers on whether it is smarter to let the market decide which businesses survive or to use taxpayer funds to artificially keep old industries alive.
stories.why_it_matters: This suggests that giving government money to car companies might be a waste. It argues that letting the market decide is better for long-term jobs and growth.
stories.other_side: Critics say stopping subsidies could cause immediate job losses. They worry that local workers will suffer before new industries can replace them.

stories.headline: Canada’s Oilpatch Shifts from Retrenchment to Expansion
stories.summary: Canadian energy producers are reporting billions in profits, leading to a significant shift in sentiment towards growth and expansion after a decade of caution. This financial turnaround is prompting several players to invest in new production capabilities, signaling a renewed confidence in the sector's profitability.
stories.original_title: ‘Excitement over growth again’: A shift in Canada’s oilpatch as some players eye expansion — Reporting billions in profits, some Canadian energy producers expect to invest in new production, a change from the past decade. Read on
stories.context: For about ten years, the oil and gas industry in Canada went through a tough period where companies were scared to spend money and focused only on staying afloat due to low prices and uncertainty. Recently, however, oil prices have stabilized and profits have surged, giving these energy companies a lot of extra cash and renewed confidence in the future. Because they are now making so much money, they are shifting their strategy from being cautious to aggressively investing in new projects to produce even more oil. This change signals that the industry believes the high profitability will continue, prompting a wave of new construction and expansion across the country.
stories.why_it_matters: Canadian oil companies are finally making big profits again. This means they will likely drill for more oil, which boosts the economy but hurts the environment.
stories.other_side: Environmental groups say this is bad news for climate goals. They argue we should stop digging up fossil fuels instead of expanding production.

stories.headline: Fortis Inc. Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
stories.summary: Fortis Inc. has released its official financial results for the second quarter of 2026, constituting a designated news release incorporated into its prospectus supplements. This disclosure provides critical data on the utility company's quarterly performance and financial health for investors.
stories.original_title: Fortis Inc. Releases Second Quarter 2026 Results — This news release constitutes a "Designated News Release" incorporated by reference in the prospectus supplement dated December 9, 2024 to Fortis' short form base shelf prospectus dated December 9, 2024.
stories.context: Fortis Inc. is a large company that provides essential services like electricity and water to millions of people, operating mostly in Canada and the Caribbean. Every three months, public companies like Fortis must release a detailed report card of their financial health, known as quarterly results, so investors can see if they are making money. The recent report for the second quarter of 2026 shows how well the company performed during those specific months, including details on revenue, expenses, and profit. These documents are critical because they help people who own stock in the company decide whether to buy, sell, or hold their shares based on the firm's stability.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a standard update on how one power company is doing. It helps investors decide if they should buy or sell their shares in the company.
stories.other_side: Regular customers might not care about these quarterly numbers. They are more focused on whether their electricity bills are going up or down.

stories.headline: Perimeter Solutions Posts $181.6M Net Loss in Q2 2026
stories.summary: Perimeter Solutions reported a second-quarter net loss of $181.6 million, though adjusted net income stood at $59.6 million. The company attributed its performance to continued value driver execution and recent acquisitions, providing key insights into its financial trajectory.
stories.original_title: Perimeter Solutions Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results — Second quarter Net Loss of $181.6M and Adjusted Net Income of $59.6M  Continued Value Driver execution and recent acquisitions drove second quarter...
stories.context: Perimeter Solutions is a global company that makes safety products, such as fire-resistant materials used in buildings and vehicles. In the second quarter of 2026, the company reported a significant loss of $181.6 million, which sounds bad at first glance, but they also showed an "adjusted" profit of nearly $60 million. This difference exists because the big loss includes one-time costs from buying other companies or writing down the value of assets, which accountants treat differently than regular daily operations. Investors look at both numbers to understand the true health of the business, separating temporary accounting hits from the actual ongoing performance of the company's core products.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that some companies lose money on paper even when they seem to be doing okay. It highlights how accounting rules can change how profits look.
stories.other_side: Investors might see this as a red flag. A large net loss can scare people away from buying the stock, even if the core business is stable.

stories.headline: BrightSpring Health Services Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance
stories.summary: BrightSpring Health Services announced its second-quarter 2026 financial results and simultaneously increased its full-year guidance. As a leading provider of home and community-based health services, this adjustment reflects management's confidence in the company's ongoing revenue generation and operational efficiency.
stories.original_title: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Increases Full Year 2026 Guidance — LOUISVILLE, Ky., July 31, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. (“BrightSpring” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: BTSG), a leading provider of home and community-based health services for complex populations, today announced financial results f…
stories.context: BrightSpring Health Services is a major provider of healthcare services, particularly focusing on helping people receive medical care at home or in their communities rather than in hospitals. When a company releases its quarterly earnings, it often updates its "guidance," which is its official prediction of how much money it expects to make for the rest of the year. By raising this guidance, BrightSpring is telling investors that it expects to earn more profit than previously thought, likely due to increased demand for home care services. This boost in confidence suggests that the company’s operations are running smoothly and that its strategy for serving patients is generating strong revenue.
stories.why_it_matters: This health service company expects to make more money this year than they first thought. It shows they are growing and becoming more efficient at helping patients.
stories.other_side: Higher costs could mean higher prices for services. Patients or insurance companies might end up paying more if the company pushes for higher revenue.

stories.headline: Capri Loans Integrates OpenAI Enterprise-Grade AI into Lending
stories.summary: Capri Loans has entered a collaboration with OpenAI to integrate enterprise-grade artificial intelligence into its lending operations. This strategic move aims to enhance operational efficiency and decision-making capabilities within the financial lending sector through advanced AI technologies.
stories.original_title: Capri Loans Collaborates with OpenAI to Bring Enterprise-Grade AI to Lending Operations
stories.context: Capri Loans is a financial company that lends money to individuals or businesses, a process that traditionally involves lots of paperwork and manual review of creditworthiness. They have partnered with OpenAI, the creators of ChatGPT, to use advanced artificial intelligence to automate and improve these lending decisions. This technology can quickly analyze vast amounts of data to assess risk and approve loans faster than humans could alone, reducing errors and speeding up service. By integrating this enterprise-grade AI, Capri aims to lower its operational costs and offer better, quicker decisions to borrowers, staying competitive in a tech-driven financial landscape.
stories.why_it_matters: Using AI in lending means loans could be approved faster and cheaper. It changes how banks work by relying on computers instead of just human judgment.
stories.other_side: People worry about privacy and bias in AI decisions. There is a risk that computer errors could unfairly deny loans to certain groups of people.

stories.headline: Zum Announces Major Investment in Philadelphia Workforce and Facilities
stories.summary: Student mobility leader Zum has announced a major investment in Philadelphia, including expanded hiring and modern facility upgrades. This financial commitment supports local families and the workforce, marking a significant capital injection into the region's educational infrastructure services.
stories.original_title: Zum Announces Major Investment in Philadelphia to Support Students, Families, and Local Workforce — Establishes long-term presence in Philadelphia, expands hiring, and invests in modern facilities as it prepares to serve School District of Philadelphia families PHILADELPHIA, July 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zum, a leader in modern student mobility, today annou…
stories.context: Zum is a company that specializes in student transportation, providing safe and reliable bus services to get children to and from school in various cities. They recently announced a major investment in Philadelphia, which includes hiring more drivers and staff while upgrading their facilities to be more modern and efficient. This move is not just about business growth; it is also a commitment to supporting the local community by creating jobs and improving the infrastructure that families rely on daily. Such investments signal that Zum sees Philadelphia as a key market for expansion and wants to strengthen its presence by directly contributing to the city's educational support system.
stories.why_it_matters: Putting money into Philadelphia creates local jobs and improves school buses. It helps families get to school safely while boosting the local economy.
stories.other_side: Some taxpayers might think this is too much government spending. They may prefer that money be used for other public services like roads or parks.

stories.headline: Mortgage Rates Drop to 6.55% as Refinancing Opportunities Grow
stories.summary: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rates have fallen by 10 basis points to 6.55%, while 15-year fixed loans are at 6.03%. This downward trend in interest rates creates new opportunities for homeowners to refinance existing debts or secure more favorable terms for new purchases.
stories.original_title: Mortgage and refinance interest rates today, Friday, July 31, 2026: Mortgage rates find more room to fall — The average 30-year fixed rate today, Friday, July 31, 2026, is 6.55%, down 10 basis points since yesterday. The 15-year fixed loan is currently at 6.03%, 4...
stories.context: A mortgage is a loan used to buy a house, and the interest rate is the extra cost you pay the bank for borrowing that money over time. Recently, the average interest rate for a standard 30-year mortgage dropped slightly to 6.55%, which means monthly payments for new homebuyers are becoming a bit more affordable. For existing homeowners, this drop creates an opportunity to "refinance," which means replacing their current loan with a new one at a lower rate to reduce their monthly bills. Even a small decrease in rates can save thousands of dollars over the life of a loan, making it an attractive time for many people to adjust their housing finances.
stories.why_it_matters: Lower mortgage rates mean it is cheaper to buy a house or lower monthly payments. This gives homeowners a chance to save money on their biggest expense.
stories.other_side: Lower rates often attract more buyers, which can push home prices up. This makes it harder for first-time buyers to afford a home despite cheaper loans.

stories.headline: Fetch Expands Student Housing Operations Across New College Markets
stories.summary: Fetch is accelerating growth in student housing by expanding its centralized service model into multiple new college markets including Ann Arbor and Austin. This expansion represents a strategic financial move to capture scalable revenue opportunities in high-demand residential sectors for operators and residents.
stories.original_title: Fetch Accelerates Student Housing Growth Across New College Markets, Expanding Scalable Community Services for Operators and Residents — Expansion into Ann Arbor, Athens, Baton Rouge, College Station, Gainesville, Knoxville, and Madison extends Fetch's centralized model for package management and valet trash in high-demand student housing markets AUSTIN, Texas, July 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fe…
stories.context: Fetch is a company that manages properties specifically designed for college students, handling everything from maintenance to tenant relations so individual owners don't have to. They are expanding their services into new college towns like Ann Arbor and Austin, where there is a high demand for student housing near universities. By centralizing their management model, Fetch can operate efficiently across many locations, offering a consistent experience for students and reliable returns for property owners. This growth strategy allows them to capture more market share in popular academic hubs, turning local housing needs into scalable business opportunities.
stories.why_it_matters: Expanding into new college towns means more housing options for students. It also brings business growth and jobs to those specific communities.
stories.other_side: Locals might worry about overcrowding and rising rents. An influx of students can strain local resources and change the character of quiet neighborhoods.
